steps.label: Parity Blocks and Checksums
steps.content:
2.2 Methods of Error Detection

Parity Blocks and Checksums

Year 10

  • Today: two more ways to check data after it is sent: the parity block check and the checksum.
  • You already know: a parity bit on each byte. This is a parity byte check.
Think → Pair → ShareA parity byte check cannot find two changed bits. Why do we need other checks?Show the answer

Some errors get past it. Another check can catch errors the first one misses.

steps.label: The Parity Block
steps.content:
The Parity Block

Think → Pair → SharePredict: even parity. The byte 01011010 is sent. Two bits change and 01101010 arrives. Does the parity byte check find the error?Show the worked answer

No. 01101010 still has four 1s: even. The row looks correct.

So we also check the columns. This is a parity block check.

  • The bytes are sent together as a block.
  • Each byte has a parity bit. It checks its row.
  • A parity byte is added at the end. Each bit of it checks one column.
  • The receiver checks every row and every column.

Even parity block

Parity bitBit 1Bit 2Bit 3Bit 4Bit 5Bit 6Bit 7
Byte 101011010
Byte 211100100
Byte 300110011
Parity byte10001101

The parity byte makes every column even.

Finding the Error

Think → Pair → SharePredict: one bit changed on the way. Which row has an odd number of 1s? Which column? Where do they cross?Show the worked answer

Byte 2 has five 1s: odd. The Bit 4 column has an odd number of 1s.

They cross at Byte 2, Bit 4. That bit was changed. Change it back: 1 becomes 0.

  • Check every row. Find the byte with the wrong number of 1s.
  • Check every column. Find the bit with the wrong number of 1s.
  • The error is where the row and the column cross.
  • The receiver can now correct the bit, or ask for the data again.

steps.label: Exam Question: Block or Byte?
steps.content:
Exam Question: Block or Byte?

Think → Pair → ShareThis has 2 marks. What two ideas do you need?Show the answer

What the parity byte check misses (two changes in one byte), and what the block adds (the columns show where).

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2023, Question 5(c)(ii). A parity block check can be used instead of a parity byte check.

items.prompt: Explain how a parity block check might detect an error in transmission that would not be detected by a parity byte check. [2]
items.modelAnswer: A parity byte check cannot detect an even number of changes in a byte (for example two bits swapped), because the parity stays correct. A parity block check also checks every column, so it identifies the horizontal and vertical position of the changes.

steps.label: The Checksum
steps.content:
The Checksum

Think → Pair → SharePredict: the sender sends 20, 35, 14 and their total, 69. The receiver gets 20, 36, 14. What does the receiver notice?Show the worked answer

The receiver adds up what arrived: 20 + 36 + 14 = 70.

70 is not 69. The values do not match, so an error is detected.

  • The sender uses an algorithm to calculate a value from the data: the checksum. Here, the algorithm adds up the values.
  • The checksum is sent with the data.
  • The receiver uses the same algorithm to recalculate the checksum.
  • The two values are compared. Different: an error is detected, and the data is sent again.

Sent: data

203514

Sent: checksum

69

Received: data

203614

Recalculated: 20 + 36 + 14 = ?

steps.label: Activity 2: Be the Receiver
steps.content:
Activity 2: Be the Receiver

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the receiver NOT just copy the checksum it received?Show the answer

It must calculate its own value from the data that arrived, or there is nothing to compare.

Be the sender: calculate the checksum. Then be the receiver: recalculate, compare and decide. New values every time.

steps.label: Exam Question: Using the Checksum
steps.content:
Exam Question: Using the Checksum

Think → Pair → ShareActivity 2 had three steps for the receiver. What were they?Show the answer

Recalculate the checksum, compare the two values, decide: same means no error, different means an error.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2026, Question 2(d). A checksum is used to check for errors in the data. A checksum value is calculated from the data before it is transmitted.

items.prompt: Describe how this checksum value is used to check for errors in the data after transmission. [3]
items.modelAnswer: Any three: the checksum value is sent with the data; the receiving device uses the same algorithm to recalculate the checksum value; the two checksum values are compared; if the checksum values are the same no error has occurred, if they are different an error has occurred.

steps.label: Exam Question: Why a Mismatch Means an Error
steps.content:
Exam Question: Why a Mismatch Means an Error

Think → Pair → ShareIf the data did NOT change, could the two values be different?Show the answer

No. The same algorithm on the same data always gives the same value.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(f)(ii). In the checksum error detection method, two values are compared after transmission. If the values do not match, an error is detected.

items.prompt: Explain why the values not matching would show an error has occurred. [2]
items.modelAnswer: Any two: the checksum is calculated from (using) the data; using the same algorithm on both sides; so if the values are different, the data must be different.
